seoTitle: Connect a GoDaddy Domain to Namecheap EasyWP Hosting
metaDescription: Point a GoDaddy domain to Namecheap EasyWP hosting for free by updating DNS records, no domain transfer required. Step-by-step connection guide.
intro: You don't need to transfer a domain away from GoDaddy just to host it on Namecheap's EasyWP platform — you can connect the two for free by updating DNS records. This guide covers logging into GoDaddy, finding your domain's DNS settings, and pointing them to EasyWP.

steps.heading: Log in to your GoDaddy account
steps.body: Access your GoDaddy account and locate the domain you want to connect to EasyWP hosting.

steps.heading: Find your domain's DNS settings
steps.body: Open the DNS management page for your domain, where you'll be replacing existing records with the ones EasyWP requires.

steps.heading: Get the DNS records from EasyWP
steps.body: In your Namecheap EasyWP dashboard, find the specific A record and any other DNS values needed to point your domain to the hosting.

steps.heading: Update the records in GoDaddy
steps.body: Replace the default GoDaddy DNS records with the EasyWP values so your domain resolves to your new hosting.

steps.heading: Verify the connection goes live
steps.body: After propagation, check that your domain now loads the site hosted on EasyWP rather than any previous GoDaddy page.

faq.question: Do I need to transfer my domain from GoDaddy to connect it to EasyWP?
faq.answer: No, you can keep the domain registered at GoDaddy and simply point its DNS records to Namecheap's EasyWP hosting.

faq.question: Is this connection method really free?
faq.answer: Yes, updating DNS records to point your existing domain to EasyWP doesn't require an additional purchase or transfer fee.

faq.question: How long before my site is live on the new hosting?
faq.answer: It depends on DNS propagation, which can take anywhere from a few minutes to a day depending on your domain and location.

faq.question: Will my email still work after changing DNS?
faq.answer: It depends on whether your email uses records tied to the same domain, so check MX records before making changes to avoid disruption.
